Contemporary knowledge suggests that some reactions previously thought to be immune-mediated are, in fact, non-immune, but in some cases can still pose a life threatening risk. It is acknowledged that many clinicians might not be in a position to distinguish the mechanism of a particular reaction. Often the term \"allergy\" is used rather generically and may overlap with the use of \"intolerance\" - in practice the boundaries between these two concepts might not be well-defined or understood. This data element is included nevertheless, because many legacy systems have captured this attribute. Immunologic testing may provide supporting evidence for the basis of the reaction and the causative substance, but no tests are 100% sensitive or specific for sensitivity to a particular substance. For example, a SNOMED coding might allow for additional specificity.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.type\\\">AllergyIntolerance.type</h3><p>Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for the reaction risk.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceType</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for a Reaction Risk.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Allergic (typically immune-mediated) reactions have been traditionally regarded as an indicator for potential escalation to significant future risk. Contemporary knowledge suggests that some reactions previously thought to be immune-mediated are, in fact, non-immune, but in some cases can still pose a life threatening risk. It is acknowledged that many clinicians might not be in a position to distinguish the mechanism of a particular reaction. Often the term \\\"allergy\\\" is used rather generically and may overlap with the use of \\\"intolerance\\\" - in practice the boundaries between these two concepts might not be well-defined or understood. This data element is included nevertheless, because many legacy systems have captured this attribute. Immunologic testing may provide supporting evidence for the basis of the reaction and the causative substance, but no tests are 100% sensitive or specific for sensitivity to a particular substance. If, as is commonly the case, it is unclear whether the reaction is due to an allergy or an intolerance, then the type element should be omitted from the resource.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.category\\\">AllergyIntolerance.category</h3><p>Category of the identified substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-category|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceCategory</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Category of an identified substance associated with allergies or intolerances.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This data element has been included because it is currently being captured in some clinical systems. This data can be derived from the substance where coding systems are used, and is effectively redundant in that situation.  When searching on category, consider the implications of AllergyIntolerance resources without a category.  For example, when searching on category = medication, medication allergies that don't have a category valued will not be returned.  Refer to <a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">search</a> for more information on how to search category with a :missing modifier to get allergies that don't have a category.  Additionally, category should be used with caution because category can be subjective based on the sender.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.criticality\\\">AllergyIntolerance.criticality</h3><p>Estimate of the potential clinical harm, or seriousness, of the reaction to the identified substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-criticality|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceCriticality</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Estimate of the potential clinical harm, or seriousness, of a reaction to an identified substance.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>The default criticality value for any propensity to an adverse reaction should be 'Low Risk', indicating at the very least a relative contraindication to deliberate or voluntary exposure to the substance. 'High Risk' is flagged if the clinician has identified a propensity for a more serious or potentially life-threatening reaction, such as anaphylaxis, and implies an absolute contraindication to deliberate or voluntary exposure to the substance. If this element is missing, the criticality is unknown (though it may be known elsewhere).  Systems that capture a severity at the condition level are actually representing the concept of criticality whereas the severity documented at the reaction level is representing the true reaction severity.  Existing systems that are capturing both condition criticality and reaction severity may use the term \\\"severity\\\" to represent both.  Criticality is the worst it could be in the future (i.e. situation-agnostic) whereas severity is situation-dependent.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.code\\\">AllergyIntolerance.code</h3><p>Code for an allergy or intolerance statement (either a positive or a negated/excluded statement).  This may be a code for a substance or pharmaceutical product that is considered to be responsible for the adverse reaction risk (e.g., \\\"Latex\\\"), an allergy or intolerance condition (e.g., \\\"Latex allergy\\\"), or a negated/excluded code for a specific substance or class (e.g., \\\"No latex allergy\\\") or a general or categorical negated statement (e.g.,  \\\"No known allergy\\\", \\\"No known drug allergies\\\").  Note: the substance for a specific reaction may be different from the substance identified as the cause of the risk, but it must be consistent with it. For instance, it may be a more specific substance (e.g. a brand medication) or a composite product that includes the identified substance. It must be clinically safe to only process the 'code' and ignore the 'reaction.substance'.  If a receiving system is unable to confirm that AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance falls within the semantic scope of AllergyIntolerance.code, then the receiving system should ignore AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>1..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://cts.nlm.nih.gov/fhir/ValueSet/2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1186.8\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">USCoreAllergyIntolerance</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#extensible\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">extensible</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>It is strongly recommended that this element be populated using a terminology, where possible. For example, some terminologies used include RxNorm, SNOMED CT, DM+D, NDFRT, ICD-9, IDC-10, UNII, and ATC. Plain text should only be used if there is no appropriate terminology available. Additional details can be specified in the text.\\n\\nWhen a substance or product code is specified for the 'code' element, the \\\"default\\\" semantic context is that this is a positive statement of an allergy or intolerance (depending on the value of the 'type' element, if present) condition to the specified substance/product.  In the corresponding SNOMED CT allergy model, the specified substance/product is the target (destination) of the \\\"Causative agent\\\" relationship.\\n\\nThe 'substanceExposureRisk' extension is available as a structured and more flexible alternative to the 'code' element for making positive or negative allergy or intolerance statements.  This extension provides the capability to make \\\"no known allergy\\\" (or \\\"no risk of adverse reaction\\\") statements regarding any coded substance/product (including cases when a pre-coordinated \\\"no allergy to x\\\" concept for that substance/product does not exist).  If the 'substanceExposureRisk' extension is present, the AllergyIntolerance.code element SHALL be omitted.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.patient\\\">AllergyIntolerance.patient</h3><p>The patient who has the allergy or intolerance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; Note: the substance for a specific reaction may be different from the substance identified as the cause of the risk, but it must be consistent with it. For instance, it may be a more specific substance (e.g. a brand medication) or a composite product that includes the identified substance. It must be clinically safe to only process the 'code' and ignore the 'reaction.substance'.  If a receiving system is unable to confirm that AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance falls within the semantic scope of AllergyIntolerance.code, then the receiving system should ignore AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">SubstanceCode</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#example\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">example</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Codes defining the type of the substance (including pharmaceutical products).</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Coding of the specific substance (or pharmaceutical product) with a terminology capable of triggering decision support should be used wherever possible.  The 'code' element allows for the use of a specific substance or pharmaceutical product, or a group or class of substances. In the case of an allergy or intolerance to a class of substances, (for example, \\\"penicillins\\\"), the 'reaction.substance' element could be used to code the specific substance that was identified as having caused the reaction (for example, \\\"amoxycillin\\\"). Duplication of the value in the 'code' and 'reaction.substance' elements is acceptable when a specific substance has been recorded in 'code'.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation\\\">AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation</h3><p>Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with the adverse reaction event.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>1..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/clinical-findings\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">SNOMEDCTClinicalFindings</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#extensible\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">extensible</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Manifestation can be expressed as a single word, phrase or brief description. For example, multiple Patient and a Person resource instance might share the same social insurance number.</p></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Requirements</span></td><td><p>Allows identification of the AllergyIntolerance as it is known by various participating systems and in a way that remains consistent across servers.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus\\\">AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus</h3><p>The clinical status of the allergy or intolerance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergyintolerance-clinical\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceClinicalStatusCodes</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Refer to <a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/extensibility.html#Special-Case\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">discussion</a> if clincalStatus is missing data.\\nThe data type is CodeableConcept because clinicalStatus has some clinical judgment involved, such that there might need to be more specificity than the required FHIR value set allows. For example, a SNOMED coding might allow for additional specificity.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus\\\">AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus</h3><p>Assertion about certainty associated with the propensity, or potential risk, of a reaction to the identified substance (including pharmaceutical product).</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergyintolerance-verification\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceVerificationStatus</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>The data type is CodeableConcept because verificationStatus has some clinical judgment involved, such that there might need to be more specificity than the required FHIR value set allows. For example, a SNOMED coding might allow for additional specificity.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.type\\\">AllergyIntolerance.type</h3><p>Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for the reaction risk.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceType</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for a Reaction Risk.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Allergic (typically immune-mediated) reactions have been traditionally regarded as an indicator for potential escalation to significant future risk. Contemporary knowledge suggests that some reactions previously thought to be immune-mediated are, in fact, non-immune, but in some cases can still pose a life threatening risk. It is acknowledged that many clinicians might not be in a position to distinguish the mechanism of a particular reaction. Often the term \\\"allergy\\\" is used rather generically and may overlap with the use of \\\"intolerance\\\" - in practice the boundaries between these two concepts might not be well-defined or understood. This data element is included nevertheless, because many legacy systems have captured this attribute. Immunologic testing may provide supporting evidence for the basis of the reaction and the causative substance, but no tests are 100% sensitive or specific for sensitivity to a particular substance. If, as is commonly the case, it is unclear whether the reaction is due to an allergy or an intolerance, then the type element should be omitted from the resource.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.category\\\">AllergyIntolerance.category</h3><p>Category of the identified substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-category|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceCategory</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Category of an identified substance associated with allergies or intolerances.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This data element has been included because it is currently being captured in some clinical systems. This data can be derived from the substance where coding systems are used, and is effectively redundant in that situation.  When searching on category, consider the implications of AllergyIntolerance resources without a category.  For example, when searching on category = medication, medication allergies that don't have a category valued will not be returned.  Refer to <a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">search</a> for more information on how to search category with a :missing modifier to get allergies that don't have a category.  Additionally, category should be used with caution because category can be subjective based on the sender.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.criticality\\\">AllergyIntolerance.criticality</h3><p>Estimate of the potential clinical harm, or seriousness, of the reaction to the identified substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-criticality|4.0.1\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">AllergyIntoleranceCriticality</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#required\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">required</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Estimate of the potential clinical harm, or seriousness, of a reaction to an identified substance.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>The default criticality value for any propensity to an adverse reaction should be 'Low Risk', indicating at the very least a relative contraindication to deliberate or voluntary exposure to the substance. 'High Risk' is flagged if the clinician has identified a propensity for a more serious or potentially life-threatening reaction, such as anaphylaxis, and implies an absolute contraindication to deliberate or voluntary exposure to the substance. If this element is missing, the criticality is unknown (though it may be known elsewhere).  Systems that capture a severity at the condition level are actually representing the concept of criticality whereas the severity documented at the reaction level is representing the true reaction severity.  Existing systems that are capturing both condition criticality and reaction severity may use the term \\\"severity\\\" to represent both.  Criticality is the worst it could be in the future (i.e. situation-agnostic) whereas severity is situation-dependent.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.code\\\">AllergyIntolerance.code</h3><p>Code for an allergy or intolerance statement (either a positive or a negated/excluded statement).  This may be a code for a substance or pharmaceutical product that is considered to be responsible for the adverse reaction risk (e.g., \\\"Latex\\\"), an allergy or intolerance condition (e.g., \\\"Latex allergy\\\"), or a negated/excluded code for a specific substance or class (e.g., \\\"No latex allergy\\\") or a general or categorical negated statement (e.g.,  \\\"No known allergy\\\", \\\"No known drug allergies\\\").  Note: the substance for a specific reaction may be different from the substance identified as the cause of the risk, but it must be consistent with it. For instance, it may be a more specific substance (e.g. a brand medication) or a composite product that includes the identified substance. It must be clinically safe to only process the 'code' and ignore the 'reaction.substance'.  If a receiving system is unable to confirm that AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance falls within the semantic scope of AllergyIntolerance.code, then the receiving system should ignore AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>1..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://cts.nlm.nih.gov/fhir/ValueSet/2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1186.8\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">USCoreAllergyIntolerance</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#extensible\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">extensible</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>It is strongly recommended that this element be populated using a terminology, where possible. For example, some terminologies used include RxNorm, SNOMED CT, DM+D, NDFRT, ICD-9, IDC-10, UNII, and ATC. Plain text should only be used if there is no appropriate terminology available. Additional details can be specified in the text.\\n\\nWhen a substance or product code is specified for the 'code' element, the \\\"default\\\" semantic context is that this is a positive statement of an allergy or intolerance (depending on the value of the 'type' element, if present) condition to the specified substance/product.  In the corresponding SNOMED CT allergy model, the specified substance/product is the target (destination) of the \\\"Causative agent\\\" relationship.\\n\\nThe 'substanceExposureRisk' extension is available as a structured and more flexible alternative to the 'code' element for making positive or negative allergy or intolerance statements.  This extension provides the capability to make \\\"no known allergy\\\" (or \\\"no risk of adverse reaction\\\") statements regarding any coded substance/product (including cases when a pre-coordinated \\\"no allergy to x\\\" concept for that substance/product does not exist).  If the 'substanceExposureRisk' extension is present, the AllergyIntolerance.code element SHALL be omitted.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.patient\\\">AllergyIntolerance.patient</h3><p>The patient who has the allergy or intolerance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; For instance, it may be a more specific substance (e.g. a brand medication) or a composite product that includes the identified substance. It must be clinically safe to only process the 'code' and ignore the 'reaction.substance'.  If a receiving system is unable to confirm that AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance falls within the semantic scope of AllergyIntolerance.code, then the receiving system should ignore AllergyIntolerance.reaction.substance.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">SubstanceCode</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#example\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">example</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>Codes defining the type of the substance (including pharmaceutical products).</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Coding of the specific substance (or pharmaceutical product) with a terminology capable of triggering decision support should be used wherever possible.  The 'code' element allows for the use of a specific substance or pharmaceutical product, or a group or class of substances. In the case of an allergy or intolerance to a class of substances, (for example, \\\"penicillins\\\"), the 'reaction.substance' element could be used to code the specific substance that was identified as having caused the reaction (for example, \\\"amoxycillin\\\"). Duplication of the value in the 'code' and 'reaction.substance' elements is acceptable when a specific substance has been recorded in 'code'.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation\\\">AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation</h3><p>Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with the adverse reaction event.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>1..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#CodeableConcept\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CodeableConcept</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/clinical-findings\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">SNOMEDCTClinicalFindings</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#extensible\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">extensible</a><span>)</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Manifestation can be expressed as a single word, phrase or brief description. For example: nausea, rash or no reaction. It is preferable that manifestation should be coded with a terminology, where possible. The values entered here may be used to display on an application screen as part of a list of adverse reactions, as recommended in the UK NHS CUI guidelines.  Terminologies commonly used include, but are not limited to, SNOMED CT or ICD10.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"AllergyIntolerance.reaction.description\\\">AllergyIntolerance.reaction.description</h3><p>Text description about the reaction as a whole, including details of the manifestation if required.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#string\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">string</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Use the description to provide any details of a particular event of the occurred reaction such as circumstances, reaction specifics, what happened before/after. None of this appears in the EHI export. There is no Claim, Coverage, ExplanationOfBenefit, or any billing-related resource type.\n- **E-prescribing data**: While MedicationRequest covers orders, there is no documentation of prescription fill status, pharmacy information, prior authorization records, or renewal histories.\n- **Patient portal/engagement data**: Secure messages, intake form submissions, patient-reported outcomes — none documented in the export.\n- **Scheduling data**: Despite myhELO having multi-device scheduling and OR resource management, appointment/scheduling data is absent.\n- **Telehealth visit records**: myhELO offers telehealth with video visits, but telehealth-specific data (session records, shared files) is not documented.\n- **Surgical templates**: myhELO emphasizes customizable surgical templates for orthopedic procedures — these specialty-specific clinical data structures are not reflected in the export.\n- **Medical images**: While DiagnosticReport can include PDF attachments, there's no specific documentation of how the built-in medical image viewing/storage/sharing capability exports image data (DICOM, etc.).\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **FHIR R4 JSON** following **US Core profiles**. This is a well-structured, standards-based approach. The 17 resource types map directly to the US Core Implementation Guide resource set, which strongly suggests this is a **g(10) FHIR API repackaged as b(10) EHI export documentation**.\n\nEvidence for this assessment:\n1. No billing data, specialty clinical data, or product-specific data domains are represented — only USCDI clinical data\n\nThe vendor's statement that they export data \"for convenience\" in FHIR format is technically accurate but obscures the gap: FHIR US Core covers the USCDI clinical data subset, not the full designated record set that b(10) requires.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths**:\n- Clean, navigable web-based documentation with a clear index page\n- Field-level definitions with cardinality, data types, and value set bindings\n- Example FHIR JSON responses for nearly all resources\n- Machine-readable CapabilityStatement and API spec available\n- USCDI elements explicitly tagged in the definitions\n- Full FHIR StructureDefinitions embedded in the JS bundle, providing computable element-level metadata\n\n**Weaknesses**:\n- All pages are JavaScript-rendered (SPA) — content is not accessible to screen readers or simple HTTP clients\n- No downloadable artifacts (no PDF, no ZIP, no schema files)\n- No documentation of the export process itself (how does a user initiate an export? what UI?)\n- No documentation of export scope selection (the intro mentions \"all or selected datasets\" but doesn't explain how)\n- No sample export files showing what a complete patient export looks like\n- Documentation is entirely FHIR standard boilerplate — there is very little vendor-specific content explaining how myhELO's data maps to these FHIR resources\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Field-level definitions with cardinality, types, and bindings — this is detailed\n- **Value sets**: Standard FHIR value sets referenced with binding strengths\n- **Relationships**: References between resources are documented (e.g., AllergyIntolerance.patient → Patient)\n- **Versioning**: CapabilityStatement shows software version 3.14, release date 2022-12-15 — but the data dictionary pages have no visible version or last-updated date\n- **Custom data**: No custom extensions, profiles, or vendor-specific elements documented — this raises the question of how product-specific data (surgical templates, billing, RCM) would be exported\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nmyhELO has built a technically competent FHIR R4 API with US Core profile conformance and has presented it as their EHI export mechanism. The documentation is well-organized with field-level definitions and example data. However, **this appears to be their g(10) FHIR API documentation relabeled as b(10) EHI export documentation**. what UI?)\n- No documentation of export scope selection (the intro mentions \"all or selected datasets\" but doesn't explain how)\n- No sample export files showing what a complete patient export looks like\n- Documentation is entirely FHIR standard boilerplate — there is very little vendor-specific content explaining how myhELO's data maps to these FHIR resources\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Field-level definitions with cardinality, types, and bindings — this is detailed\n- **Value sets**: Standard FHIR value sets referenced with binding strengths\n- **Relationships**: References between resources are documented (e.g., AllergyIntolerance.patient → Patient)\n- **Versioning**: CapabilityStatement shows software version 3.14, release date 2022-12-15 — but the data dictionary pages have no visible version or last-updated date\n- **Custom data**: No custom extensions, profiles, or vendor-specific elements documented — this raises the question of how product-specific data (surgical templates, billing, RCM) would be exported\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nmyhELO has built a technically competent FHIR R4 API with US Core profile conformance and has presented it as their EHI export mechanism. The documentation is well-organized with field-level definitions and example data. However, **this appears to be their g(10) FHIR API documentation relabeled as b(10) EHI export documentation**. The export covers only the USCDI clinical data subset — approximately the same 17 US Core resource types that every certified EHR must expose via g(10).\n\nFor a product that bills itself as a \"Healthcare Operating System\" with integrated EMR, scheduling, RCM, patient portal, e-prescribing, and telehealth, the absence of billing data, scheduling data, patient engagement data, specialty clinical data (surgical templates), and telehealth records from the EHI export represents a significant coverage gap. The designated record set for myhELO's users (orthopedic practices and ASCs) would include procedure-specific clinical data, surgical planning records, billing/claims data, and patient-reported outcomes — none of which appear in this export.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.myhelo.com/api_export_format/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: yes (JavaScript SPA — content not accessible via curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (main page) + one_click (dataset specs)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (but JS rendering required)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- All pages on myhelo.com are JS-rendered SPAs using a 3.3MB JavaScript library (\"Rocket\"). The HTML source for every page contains only analytics scripts and an empty `<body>` tag. Browser rendering is required to see any content.\n- The FHIR well-known endpoint (`provider.myhelo.com/fhir/.well-known/fhir.json`) returns the full API spec as structured JSON — this was the most valuable machine-readable artifact found.\n- No downloadable files (PDF, ZIP, CSV, schema) were found anywhere on the site.\n- The API Docs page footer links to the same `/api/` URL as the footer of the EHI export pages, suggesting these are part of the same documentation site.\n"}}

organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care for a patient.</p><h2>Overview</h2><p>The CareTeam includes all the people, teams, and organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care for a patient. CareTeam can also be organizationally assigned without a subject in context, such as a code blue team or emergency response team. This is not limited to practitioners, but may include other caregivers such as family members, guardians, the patient themself, or others.</p><p>This profile is used to define the content that will be returned by the API Server in response to requests to access CareTeam resources. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#uri\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">uri</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.language\\\\\\\">CareTeam.language</h3><p>The base language in which the resource is written.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">CommonLanguages</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#preferred\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">preferred</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>A human language.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.text\\\\\\\">CareTeam.text</h3><p>A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it \\\\\\\"clinically safe\\\\\\\" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/narrative.html#Narrative\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Narrative</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a \\\\\\\"text blob\\\\\\\" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.contained\\\\\\\">CareTeam.contained</h3><p>These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, and nor can they have their own independent transaction scope.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/resource.html#resource\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Resource</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.\\\\n\\\\nModifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/extensibility.html#Extension\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Extension</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions. organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care for a patient.</p><h2>Overview</h2><p>The CareTeam includes all the people, teams, and organizations who plan to participate in the coordination and delivery of care for a patient. CareTeam can also be organizationally assigned without a subject in context, such as a code blue team or emergency response team. This is not limited to practitioners, but may include other caregivers such as family members, guardians, the patient themself, or others.</p><p>This profile is used to define the content that will be returned by the API Server in response to requests to access CareTeam resources. All elements described in the Definition and Detailed Definitions below are supported, which means that the API Server is capable of supplying these fields from the product database when they have been populated via the product or its APIs.</p><p>List of profiles we support:</p><ul><li><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition/us-core-careteam\\\\\\\" CareTeam</span></div></td></tr></tbody></table><br><br><h2>Detailed Definitions</h2><br><div><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam\\\\\\\">CareTeam</h3><p>\\\\\\\\-</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#id\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">id</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>The only time that a resource does not have an id is when it is being submitted to the server using a create operation.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.meta\\\\\\\">CareTeam.meta</h3><p>The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/resource.html#Meta\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Meta</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.implicitRules\\\\\\\">CareTeam.implicitRules</h3><p>A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#uri\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">uri</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.language\\\\\\\">CareTeam.language</h3><p>The base language in which the resource is written.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">CommonLanguages</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#preferred\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">preferred</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>A human language.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.text\\\\\\\">CareTeam.text</h3><p>A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it \\\\\\\"clinically safe\\\\\\\" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/narrative.html#Narrative\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Narrative</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a \\\\\\\"text blob\\\\\\\" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.contained\\\\\\\">CareTeam.contained</h3><p>These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, and nor can they have their own independent transaction scope.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/resource.html#resource\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Resource</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags In their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.extension\\\\\\\">CareTeam.extension</h3><p>May be used to represent additional information that is not part of the basic definition of the resource. To make the use of extensions safe and manageable, there is a strict set of governance  applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer can define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/extensibility.html#Extension\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Extension</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions. Usually modifier elements provide negation or qualification. To make the use of extensions safe and manageable, there is a strict set of governance applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer is allowed to define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension. Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.\\\\n\\\\nModifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/extensibility.html#Extension\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Extension</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.</p></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Requirements</span></td><td><p>Modifier extensions allow for extensions that *cannot* be safely ignored to be clearly distinguished from the vast majority of extensions which can be safely ignored.  This promotes interoperability by eliminating the need for implementers to prohibit the presence of extensions. For further information, see the <a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/extensibility.html#modifierExtension\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">definition of modifier extensions</a>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\\\\\"CareTeam.identifier\\\\\\\">CareTeam.identifier</h3><p>Business identifiers assigned to this care team by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.</p><table width=\\\\\\\"100%\\\\\\\" cellpadding=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" cellspacing=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" border=\\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\" style=\\\\\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#Identifier\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">Identifier</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\\\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\\\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier (see <a href=\\\\\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resource.html#identifiers\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">discussion</a>). Condition</span></div></td></tr></tbody></table><br><br><h2>Detailed Definitions</h2><br><div><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition\\\">Condition</h3><p>The US Core Condition Profile is based upon the core FHIR Condition Resource and created to meet the 2015 Edition Common Clinical Data Set 'Problems' and 'Health Concerns' requirements.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div></div><div></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.id\\\">Condition.id</h3><p>The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#string\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">string</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>The only time that a resource does not have an id is when it is being submitted to the server using a create operation.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.meta\\\">Condition.meta</h3><p>The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/resource.html#Meta\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Meta</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.implicitRules\\\">Condition.implicitRules</h3><p>A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#uri\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">uri</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.language\\\">Condition.language</h3><p>The base language in which the resource is written.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#code\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">code</a></div><div><span>Binding: </span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">CommonLanguages</a><span> (</span><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/terminologies.html#preferred\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">preferred</a><span>)</span><span>: </span><span>A human language.</span></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.text\\\">Condition.text</h3><p>A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it \\\"clinically safe\\\" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/narrative.html#Narrative\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Narrative</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a \\\"text blob\\\" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.contained\\\">Condition.contained</h3><p>These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, and nor can they have their own independent transaction scope.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/resource.html#resource\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Resource</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags In their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.extension\\\">Condition.extension</h3><p>May be used to represent additional information that is not part of the basic definition of the resource. To make the use of extensions safe and manageable, there is a strict set of governance  applied to the definition and use of extensions. Usually modifier elements provide negation or qualification. To make the use of extensions safe and manageable, there is a strict set of governance applied to the definition and use of extensions. Though any implementer is allowed to define an extension, there is a set of requirements that SHALL be met as part of the definition of the extension. Applications processing a resource are required to check for modifier extensions.\\n\\nModifier extensions SHALL NOT change the meaning of any elements on Resource or DomainResource (including cannot change the meaning of modifierExtension itself).</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/extensibility.html#Extension\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Extension</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>There can be no stigma associated with the use of extensions by any application, project, or standard - regardless of the institution or jurisdiction that uses or defines the extensions.  The use of extensions is what allows the FHIR specification to retain a core level of simplicity for everyone.</p></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Requirements</span></td><td><p>Modifier extensions allow for extensions that *cannot* be safely ignored to be clearly distinguished from the vast majority of extensions which can be safely ignored.  This promotes interoperability by eliminating the need for implementers to prohibit the presence of extensions. For further information, see the <a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/extensibility.html#modifierExtension\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">definition of modifier extensions</a>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><br><hr><br><h3 id=\\\"Condition.identifier\\\">Condition.identifier</h3><p>Business identifiers assigned to this condition by the performer or other systems which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..*</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#Identifier\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Identifier</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier (see <a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/resource.html#identifiers\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">discussion</a>). This is called \\\"abatement\\\" because of the many overloaded connotations associated with \\\"remission\\\" or \\\"resolution\\\" - Conditions are never really resolved, but they can abate.</p><table width=\\\"100%\\\" cellpadding=\\\"0\\\" cellspacing=\\\"0\\\" border=\\\"0\\\" style=\\\"table-layout: auto; width: auto;\\\"><tbody><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Cardinality</span></td><td><span>0..1</span></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Type</span></td><td><div><div><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#dateTime\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">dateTime</a><br><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#Age\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Age</a><br><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#Period\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Period</a><br><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#Range\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">Range</a><br><a href=\\\"http://hl7.org/fhir/r4/datatypes.html#string\\\" target=\\\"_blank\\\">string</a></div><div></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><span style=\\\"font-weight: bold;\\\">Comments</span></td><td><p>There is no explicit distinction between resolution and remission because in many cases the distinction is not clear.
